title: Masking, paths and strokes
objective: Generalize the path primitives before Corrections needs them.
context_summary: Masks run on the one action path through typed commands and a component-kind table; brush strokes are captured on the stored grid, decimated, refused at the occupancy cap where they are painted and stored by content address; every kind passes one kind-conformance suite against its frozen reference, and the studies live in the reference crate. What remains is roadmap groundwork, blocked until Corrections starts: path primitives a second stroke-carrying consumer can share.

tasks.description: Generalize the path primitives so a second stroke-carrying consumer can share them: a content-addressed store keyed by consumer-declared stroke types, and draft targets from declared identity parameters.
extra_context: Blocked: starts with the Corrections brush-based repair work; do not begin until that work starts.

`path.rs` holds the grid, the decimation (`decimate`, and `PathCapture`, which the desktop brush pushes one position at a time), `Stroke`, `StrokeId` and the content-addressed `StrokeTable`, and most of it names no mask. What still does: `path.rs` imports `mask::{REFINE_MAX, REFINE_MIN}` for `ColourLimit`, a stroke's colour limit in the domain of the operation the mask modulates, and defines `SIZE_MIN` as `mask::DISTANCE_MIN`; `StrokeTable` holds only `path::Stroke`; `Recipe::stroke_references` (`model.rs`) finds strokes from mask components only, as the owner decided until a second consumer exists; the core `Draft.target` field (`draft.rs`) is an optional `MaskTarget`, which `EditorService::draft_target` (`editor/plan.rs`) builds for host mask commands and module actions alike; and on the desktop the brush gesture (`mask_draft/brush.rs`) drives `mask.add-stroke` alone, through `commands::ADD_STROKE`, while `draft_begin_params` (`app/tasks.rs`) takes a `MaskTarget`. docs/design/masking.md ("One brush system") and docs/design/corrections.md describe these primitives as shared, which the code supports only for the path kind, the decimation and the store.

Masks must keep working unchanged once the primitives generalize: the same content-addressed store, the same stroke addresses, bit-identical coverage, and the fresh-only commit write, in which a commit writes only the referenced strokes the table does not already know are stored (`insert_stored`, `mark_stored`, `is_known_stored`).
Update docs/design/masking.md and docs/design/corrections.md to describe the shared primitive as the code now actually supports it.

acceptance_criteria: path.rs carries no mask-specific import or type; each consumer, including the mask brush, declares its own stroke payload and colour or limit semantics.
The content-addressed store holds consumer-declared stroke types, not only the mask's own Stroke, and a commit still writes only the strokes the store does not already hold, for every consumer.

Draft.target is taken from an action's declared identity parameters, checked as `check_target` and `ParameterKind::is_identity` already check them, rather than a fixed MaskTarget; MaskTarget leaves draft.rs.
Masks use the generalized store and draft target unchanged: the same stroke content addresses and bit-identical coverage.
docs/design/masking.md and docs/design/corrections.md describe the shared primitive as the code now supports it.

steps: Move the mask-specific colour-limit and radius logic out of path.rs and into the mask module's own stroke type.
Widen Draft.target to an action's declared identity parameters and update draft_target's and the desktop's mask-specific handling.
Re-run the full mask test suite to confirm identical stroke content addresses, coverage and fresh-only writes.
expected_results: Every existing mask test passes unchanged, with the same stroke content addresses and bit-identical coverage.
A second consumer can declare its own stroke type against the same store.
